title: Simulation-Ready Compositional 3D Scene Reconstruction from a Single Image
claim: Naively composed single-image lifters collapse or misplace objects under physics; correcting shape and pose with simulation feedback yields stable scenes.
layout: 3 input rows left, arrow to side-by-side baseline vs ours simulator grid, red zoom boxes
description: Three rows show scenes: a desk with monitor, laptop and books; a shelf of bottles; a pen holder with pen and eraser. The left columns show the input photo and the SAM3D reconstruction before simulation. An arrow leads to a large framed panel labeled 'Physics Simulator', split by a vertical divider into SAM3D on the left and SimuScene on the right. Each row has two rendered views per method on a checkered floor. SAM3D results show the monitor fallen under the desk, bottles tumbling out of the shelf, and the pen lying on the floor. SimuScene results show the monitor upright on the desk and bottles and pen resting stably. Red boxes with dashed zoom lines highlight corrected shapes. The eye goes first to the red-boxed desk row.
caption: \modelname reconstructs simulation-ready compositional 3D scenes from a single image by using physics simulation to correct object shape and pose. Compared with conventional 3D lifters such as SAM3D [ref], our method handles heavy occlusion and produces stable layouts. Red boxes highlight physics-guided shape corrections.
abstract: Reconstructing interactive, simulation-ready 3D scenes from a single image is a critical bottleneck for robotic manipulation. While recent single-image lifters recover plausible per-object shapes, composing them yields scenes that collapse under physical simulation due to interpenetrating, hovering, or sinking objects. Existing physics-aware compositional reconstruction methods mainly address this as a post-hoc layout correction, leaving the underlying geometric errors unresolved. To address this, we introduce SimuScene, a compositional 3D reconstruction pipeline that puts physics in the loop of shape and layout estimation. Rather than using physics merely for layout cleanup, we utilize the physics engine as a diagnostic measurement tool during the generative process itself. By diagnostically simulating reconstructed objects under gravity, we convert penetration and support failures into quantitative correction signals that drive amodal shape resampling, with gravity-axis stretching as a lightweight correction for minor errors. This physics-informed feedback loop mitigates accumulated reconstruction errors and produces a stable, simulation-ready compositional 3D scene. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on physical stability and geometric alignment benchmarks. We further highlight SimuScene's utility by deploying reconstructed environments in humanoid control and robot-arm manipulation tasks.
